subject: computer-science

moments.title: JavaScript in 10 days
moments.body: Eich writes the first version of JavaScript (originally LiveScript, renamed for marketing reasons to associate with Java) in 10 days in May 1995. The language ships in Netscape Navigator 2.0 in September. ECMAScript standardisation (Ecma International) follows in 1997.
moments.takeaway: The most-used programming language in the world was designed in 10 days under marketing pressure. Many of its quirks reflect that timeline.

moments.title: Node.js
moments.body: Dahl releases Node.js, embedding Google's V8 JavaScript engine on the server with non-blocking I/O. JavaScript becomes a full-stack language. npm (2010) becomes the largest package registry in any language. The frontend/backend language unification is a major industry shift.
moments.takeaway: JavaScript escaped the browser. A single language now runs both ends of most web applications and many desktop apps (Electron).

now.title: JavaScript today
now.body: TypeScript (Microsoft, 2012) adds static types to JavaScript and is now the default for new web projects. React (Facebook 2013), Vue (2014), Angular (Google) compete for frontend mindshare. Deno (2018, by Ryan Dahl as a Node successor) and Bun (2022) compete with Node.
now.open_questions: Will WebAssembly replace JavaScript for performance-sensitive web code? Adoption is gradual.

reflection: Eich was forced to step down as Mozilla CEO in 2014 over personal political donations. The architect of the web's most-used language was removed from leading its most-used browser by the community he built. Open source has political dimensions.
